main_body: Tall three-storey brick townhouse with a slate mansard roof, a dormer, an orange cornice, stone-framed windows and a green door
top_band: Grey-green flat roof surface at rows ~10-22, then slate roof slope in blue-grey at rows ~22-42, ending in an orange cornice band at rows ~42-46
evidence: Reading down the centre column: the grey-green roof top surface and the slate roof slope are several rows tall and clearly lit as horizontal or sloped surfaces. The orange cornice acts as a distinct front-edge line, with a dark shadow row directly under it. The brick front face below carries stone-framed windows with sills and a recessed door, plus a balcony ledge. The roof reads as a real surface, not a 1-2px rim, so this is a 3/4 building, though the mansard is steep.

style.evidence: The brick has about 5 tones with per-brick variation and mortar. The slate roof has courses with several blue-grey steps. The stone window frames and lit-window glow add further ramps. Outlines lean dark brown or navy-tinted beside the neighbouring material rather than neutral black. Texture is dense and no large flat areas appear, apart from a few small wall strips. Overall it sits comparably to the Beodeul house references.
